text:
Alex: Heads up — since last night we've seen a spike in gpu pod evictions and weird packing where some nodes have 1 GPU free but pods still can't schedule. Logs point to mixed instance types and AZ spread.
Priya: Can you paste the scheduler logs / pod events? Is this the same cluster where we added the A100-80GB and A10G nodes?
Alex: Yep that cluster. Event snippet: 
```
Warning  FailedScheduling  pod/my-infer-xyz  0/12 nodes are available: 8 node(s) had insufficient resources, 3 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
Omar: That message is generic. From `kubectl describe node` on one host we see label topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west-2b and node.gpu.type=a10g while some older nodes are a100-80. Scheduler scoring seems to prefer binpack by memory only, not by GPU type affinity.
Casey: We configured `balanced-alloc` scoring last month to reduce tail latency, but it doesn't handle heterogeneous GPU SKUs. Result: pods requiring 16GB GPU memory get spread and then cache/kv gets wasted.
Alex: infra-bot just posted a capacity alert: `capacity/fragmentation > 0.55` for that fleet.
infra-bot: [auto] Capacity fragmentation alert for cluster-infer-usw2 — free_gpus=14, free_nodes_with_gpus=9, avg_free_gpu_per_free_node=1.6 — consider compaction or pool resizing. :warning:
Priya: Short term: we can set nodeAffinity on large-model nodegroups and add tolerations so high-memory model pods prefer A100s. Longer term we need scheduler plugin or topology-aware provisioning.
Jordan: What about creating "compact" node pools (single SKU, single AZ) and labeling them with `node.k8s.redwood/pack-group=compact-a100-usw2b` then a mutating admission that adds preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity for high-priority pods?
Omar: That helps new pods but not ones already running. Eviction churn will continue until we drain low-priority jobs. We could add a draining job that consolidates interruptible work into spot-pools with a lower priority class.
Casey: Proposal sketch: 
- create compact pools for each large SKU per AZ
- schedule low-priority batch work into spot pools with `priorityClassName: best-effort-spot`
- update scheduler config: add a custom scoring plugin that rewards same-sku and same-az for GPU requests
- add an admission controller to inject `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` for pods with annotation `redwood/packable=true`

Example priority class:
```
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: best-effort-spot
value: 100
globalDefault: false
description: "For interruptible batch jobs that should be packed onto spot capacity"
```
Alex: Cost question — compact pools might increase reserved/underutilized capacity. Any rough numbers?
Priya: Quick calc: if we reserve 8 nodes of a100 (8x A100-80GB) at $3.10/hr each to reduce fragmentation by 30% -> delta monthly ~$3k but token cost saving from fewer cross-node KV misses could offset. Need proper costing run.
Omar: Also watch cross-AZ network egress — when models are sharded across AZs latency and cost go up. We should bias scheduling to keep model shards in same AZ or fallback to smaller replicas.
Jordan: Action items: 1) Priya to spin up compact-a100-usw2b pool as a canary (Q: size 4?). 2) Casey to draft scheduler plugin PR and short-lived op for admission mutating webhook. 3) Omar to prepare drain-and-consolidate playbook for low-priority pods. 4) Alex to run cost sim and post in #eng-finance.
Priya: I'll start the pool at size=4 and label it. Will tag infra change for schedule window tonight.
Casey: I'll put a minimal scoring patch that adds +100 pref score for same-gpu-type label and +50 for same-az, test on canary cluster.
Omar: For the drain playbook I'll target pods with `priorityClassName!=system-cluster-critical` and `redwood/packable=true` first. Using `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` scripted with retries.
Alex: Cool. Let's meet tomorrow 09:30 PT to review canary metrics (fragmentation, eviction-rate, p90 schedule latency). Thanks all :thumbsup:
